baseline_models.focus_anchor: The doubled feeding root in يُطْعِمُونَ ٱلطَّعَامَ and the construction عَلَىٰ حُبِّهِ.
baseline_models.mechanism: Feeding is an outward transfer, while love is attachment that clings to the heart. The construction presents the transfer as occurring while that attachment remains live, so the act costs the giver something desired rather than disposing of surplus.

activation_trace.role: Giving food to another supplies the concrete outward transfer at the center of the mechanism.
Love as clinging attachment supplies the resistance that makes handing over the food costly.

changed_reading.after: They hand over food while it still grips their affection, making relinquished attachment part of the gift.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The coordinated recipient sequence مِسْكِينًا وَيَتِيمًا وَأَسِيرًا.
baseline_models.mechanism: The three recipients embody different failures of support: material abasement, severance from a protecting parent, and coercive confinement. One meal crosses economic, kinship, and custodial boundaries rather than addressing an undifferentiated class of need.

activation_trace.role: Poverty and humble abasement identify a recipient whose material agency has collapsed.
The child cut off from a protecting parent supplies the failure of kin-based support.
Binding and captivity supply the recipient whose access is constrained by another's control.

changed_reading.before: The verse lists three examples of needy people.
changed_reading.after: The meal deliberately enters three distinct breakdowns of human support: poverty, lost protection, and imposed restraint.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The pairing of ٱلطَّعَامَ with مِسْكِينًا.
baseline_models.mechanism: Food can be livelihood and good condition, while the poor-person root includes provision that makes remaining in place possible. Feeding therefore restores a condition for stable inhabitation, not merely a momentary intake of calories.

activation_trace.role: Food as provision and livelihood expands the object from a meal into a condition of maintained life.
Provision that enables staying makes stability the practical effect of feeding the miskin.

changed_reading.after: Food gives the materially immobilized person enough provision to remain, settle, and sustain a place in life.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The final recipient أَسِيرًا read through the packet's split inventory for ء س ر.
baseline_models.mechanism: Alongside literal captivity, the root inventory offers the strength and cohesion of bodily joints. That distant branch lets the captive appear not only as a status but as a nourishable human frame whose cohesion remains vulnerable.

activation_trace.role: The cohesive bodily frame supplies an embodied underside to the otherwise social label captive.
Taking in nourishment supplies what the captive's bodily frame materially requires.

changed_reading.before: The captive is the third social category receiving food.
changed_reading.after: The captive is also exposed as a shared human body whose joined frame depends on nourishment.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediately preceding fulfillment of a self-imposed vow turns the loved-food transfer into performed commitment. Affection supplies the cost, while fulfillment carries a prior obligation all the way into a meal for people lacking support.

activation_trace.role: Feeding another is the concrete deed through which the commitment is discharged.
Clinging attachment makes fulfillment costly rather than merely formal.
Completion without deficiency frames the following meal as an obligation carried through fully.
A voluntarily assumed obligation supplies the binding commitment behind the action.

structural_cues: The plural verbs of 76:7 and 76:8 have the same unstated agents, and the feeding follows as the next coordinated action.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies vow, full performance, and an adjacent feeding action; I infer that the meal can instantiate the vow. A live alternative is that vow-keeping and feeding are parallel virtues with no one-to-one relation.

changed_reading.before: The feeding is a spontaneous generous act.
changed_reading.after: The feeding can be the bodily completion of a chosen commitment, fulfilled precisely where attachment makes it costly.

context_deltas.mechanism: Earlier chains and collars establish a punitive material field of restraint; the focus later places a bound person on the receiving side of care. The shift separates the condition of being restrained from a judgment that the restrained person deserves deprivation.

activation_trace.role: The bound captive anchors the changed reading in the final recipient.
Connected chain links establish one visible apparatus of punitive restraint.
A collar that binds a limb intensifies the material resemblance between punishment imagery and captivity.

structural_cues: The whole-surah sequence moves from bound objects in 76:4 to a bound human recipient in 76:8.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two restraint images and then a captive who is fed; I infer that care crosses the chapter's punitive visual field and refuses guilt by appearance. The alternative is that the two bondage scenes are unrelated.

changed_reading.before: The captive is simply one more needy recipient.
changed_reading.after: Feeding the captive refuses to treat visible restraint as proof of moral desert and carries care across an enemy-or-punishment boundary.

context_deltas.mechanism: The next ayah restates feeding, gives it an orientation, exposes the will behind it, and negates both recompense and recognition from the recipients. The loved object is therefore transferred without converting vulnerability into social debt.

activation_trace.role: The focus feeding anchors the motive analysis in the same material act.
Attachment identifies what the giver relinquishes without acquiring a claim on the recipient.
The repeated feeding root identifies the voiced motive with the focus action.
Face as direction supplies an orientation beyond the recipients' response.
Will and desire make the refusal of return an intentional motive rather than an accidental result.
Recompense for an action names the material return explicitly declined from recipients.
Recognition of benefit names the affective return explicitly declined from recipients.

structural_cues: 76:9 immediately follows the recipient list, repeats the first-person plural feeding verb, and uses إِنَّمَا plus two coordinated negations.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated feeding, directional motive, and denied returns; I infer that the speakers disclose the same feeders' operative intent. A live alternative is that 76:9 gives an idealized rationale rather than reported speech.

changed_reading.before: A costly gift may still create gratitude or obligation toward the giver.
changed_reading.after: The gift bears its own cost while deliberately shielding poor, orphaned, and captive recipients from repayment and gratitude debt.

context_deltas.mechanism: The returns refused from recipients in 76:9 reappear in 76:22 as reward for the givers and recognition of their striving. Reciprocity is not erased; it is relocated away from those whose need would make repayment coercive.

activation_trace.role: The feeding act is the concrete expenditure whose return architecture changes across the surah.
Action-for-action recompense is first denied as a claim against the recipients.
Grateful recognition is likewise removed from the recipients' obligations.
The same recompense image returns as an announced outcome for the givers.
The same recognition image returns with the givers' striving as its object.

structural_cues: The paired nouns جَزَاء and شُكُور in 76:9 recur in reverse grammatical relation as جَزَاء and مَشْكُور in 76:22.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a conspicuous refusal-and-return lexical pattern; I infer a relocation of reciprocity from vulnerable humans to divine acknowledgment. The alternative is that 76:22 rewards the whole conduct cluster without singling out feeding.

changed_reading.after: Pure giving abolishes claims on vulnerable recipients while allowing recompense and recognition to return from a non-coerced source.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus agents actively serve food; later vessels and attendants circulate around them and they are given drink. The direction of service reverses while preserving the same nourishment-and-hospitality domain.

activation_trace.role: Giving food to others fixes the protagonists' initial role as active servers.
Circulation around them spatially relocates service toward the former feeders.
Giving drink makes the former agents grammatical and material recipients of nourishment.
A second circulation image stabilizes the reversed service arrangement.
Their Lord's giving drink completes the reversal at its highest source.

structural_cues: The active plural وَيُطْعِمُونَ in 76:8 is answered by passive يُطَافُ عَلَيْهِمْ and يُسْقَوْنَ in 76:15-17, then an explicit giver in 76:21.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies reversed grammatical roles inside one hospitality domain; I infer that later service mirrors and honors the earlier feeding. The alternative is that the banquet is general reward imagery without act-specific mirroring.

changed_reading.before: The feeders occupy a one-way role of serving others.
changed_reading.after: Their chosen service inaugurates a reversal in which the feeders themselves become surrounded, served, and given drink.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus holds love beside relinquished food; later the same love root is condemned when fixed on what is immediate. Feeding becomes a counter-pattern in which attachment is not denied but redirected away from immediate possession toward vulnerable others.

activation_trace.role: Clinging love supplies the live attachment borne by the focus action.
Handing food outward gives attachment a direction away from possession.
The repeated clinging-love image creates a direct contrast with the focus use.
Haste and precedence identify immediacy as the rival object to which love can be misdirected.

structural_cues: 76:27 predicates the same love root of those who prefer ٱلْعَاجِلَةَ and leave a heavy day behind.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies love in both locations and names immediacy only in the later one; I infer that the focus stages disciplined love as a counter-pattern. A live alternative is that the pronoun in حُبِّهِ refers to God or to feeding rather than to the food.

changed_reading.before: The verse praises generosity despite fondness for a particular object.
changed_reading.after: The verse models love being rerouted from immediate possession into release toward people whose need cannot wait.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus's captive sense of ء س ر is later met by the same root as the cohesive bodily frame that God created and strengthened. The echo moves the captive from an alien legal status into shared creaturely embodiment: this restrained person has the same joined frame that nourishment sustains.

activation_trace.role: Binding and captivity anchor the ordinary social identity of the final recipient.
Taking nourishment supplies the bodily dependence shared across social statuses.
Created existence places the captive inside the same creaturely origin as the surrounding human plural.
Strength and solidity activate the body's need for maintained cohesion.
The strength and joining of bodily limbs supplies the explicit embodied counterpart to captive.

structural_cues: أَسِيرًا in 76:8 and أَسْرَهُمْ in 76:28 repeat the same packet root while shifting from a singular recipient to the frame of the human plural.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the root echo and both branch senses; I infer that the later bodily use can humanize the earlier captive. The live alternative is ordinary polysemy with no intended cross-activation.

changed_reading.before: The captive is defined by who holds him.
changed_reading.after: The captive is recognized as a created, joined human frame like every other body, and feeding answers that shared dependence.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus inventories let حُبّ flash as seed-grain and food as fruit reaching ripeness. Later fruit is near, made tractable, and ready to pick. On that material analogy, food surrendered as a loved seed returns as an accessible yield rather than disappearing in consumption.

activation_trace.role: Seed-grain gives the loved object an exploratory planted-potential image.
Fruit ripening and taking flavor supplies the maturation stage of the analogy.
Nearness brings the later yield within reach of those who first relinquished food.
Making difficult access easy turns the yield into provision freely available to them.
The arrival of harvest time completes the seed-to-yield sequence.

structural_cues: The focus's loved food precedes the garden sequence, where fruit is described as near and deliberately made easy to gather.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies seed, ripening, nearness, facilitation, and harvest images; I supply the arrow from surrendered food to returned yield. A live alternative is that these are independent branch images joined only by the broad food domain.

changed_reading.before: Loved food is consumed and materially gone once given.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the surrendered food behaves like seed: its attachment is planted, ripens, and returns as a yield made near and easy.

context_deltas.mechanism: The close of the surah opposes entry into mercy to punishment whose root inventory includes withholding and weaning from something. Against that endpoint, feeding the three exposed recipients becomes a local anti-withholding mechanism: mercy takes material form as allowing nourishment to pass.

activation_trace.role: Giving food is the focus act that reverses material withholding.
Mercy and tenderness supply the inclusive pole into which feeding is functionally aligned.
Withholding and weaning supply a branch-level deprivation mechanism opposed by feeding.

structural_cues: The final ayah juxtaposes entry into mercy with prepared punishment, while the focus admits three socially exposed recipients to food.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies mercy, withholding, and feeding; I infer that the focus act can miniaturize the mercy/withholding opposition in material practice. The alternative is that the punishment root's withholding branch is inactive in 76:31.

changed_reading.before: Feeding is one charitable transfer within the righteous conduct list.
changed_reading.after: Feeding becomes an embodied refusal of withholding, a small enactment of merciful inclusion before the surah's final division.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the technical grafting branch of ط ع م rather than the ordinary feeding sense. It remains anchored in the focus's feeding root, the orphan's severance, the captive's binding, and provision that enables staying. Downstream prose should present it only as a material analogy for social reattachment, never as the lexical translation of يُطْعِمُونَ.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: يُطْعِمُونَ directed toward the miskin, orphan, and captive.

activation_trace.role: A graft accepting an inserted branch supplies the cross-domain image of nourishment taking hold.
Provision that permits staying supplies the stable host condition produced by the graft-like meal.
Severance from a protecting parent supplies one form of social detachment to be rejoined.
Captive binding supplies the immobilized life that needs a sustaining connection.

changed_reading.before: The meal reaches three detached or constrained individuals.
changed_reading.after: As a contained material analogy, the meal is a graft through which detached lives can take hold again in a sustaining social body.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is branch-distant because حَرِيرًا denotes silk in 76:12 while the activated ح ر ر branch is freedom opposed to bondage. It remains relevant through the focus's explicitly bound captive and the short sequence from feeding to reward. Downstream prose must call it a latent freedom echo in the root inventory, not claim that silk lexically means emancipation here.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The captive أَسِيرًا as a bound recipient of food.

activation_trace.role: Binding and captivity establish the condition whose reversal is explored.
Freedom opposed to servitude supplies a latent release image beneath the awarded silk.

changed_reading.before: Feeding relieves a captive without changing the fact of captivity.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, care for the bound person opens a freedom trajectory whose reward sequence carries a branch-level echo of release.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it depends on the packet's non-dominant ء س ر to س ر ر mapping and must not be used to redefine أَسِيرًا as joyful. It remains inspectably anchored by the shared mapped root and branch B010 at the focus captive and the later explicit سُرُورًا. Downstream prose should label it a mapping-induced reversal from bound recipient to encountered joy, not ordinary morphology.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: أَسِيرًا through the packet's non-dominant mapped inventory root_000697.

activation_trace.role: The split inventory's joy and ease branch places a tightly contained latent counter-image under the captive.
Explicit joy and ease later realize the same mapped branch as an outcome encountered by the givers.

changed_reading.before: The final recipient closes the list in the image of confinement.
changed_reading.after: Within the packet's split mapping only, the list's captive edge is answered by a later movement into joy and ease.

strongest_changes: The immediate sequel turns costly feeding into an oriented gift that refuses to make vulnerable recipients repay or praise the giver.
The reward-and-thanks vocabulary later returns to the givers, relocating reciprocity instead of abolishing it.
The hospitality sequence reverses roles: those who actively feed become those around whom service circulates and to whom drink is given.
The later contrast with love of the immediate recasts عَلَىٰ حُبِّهِ as disciplined attachment redirected toward needs that cannot wait.
The recurrence of ء س ر as the strengthened bodily frame humanizes the captive as shared created embodiment rather than an alien status.
summary.what_was_special: The whole-surah packet produced unusually coherent reversals of debt, service direction, attachment, restraint, and embodiment. Its split ء س ر inventory also preserved non-dominant frame and joy activations that a single-sense reading would lose.
remaining_uncertainties: The antecedent of the pronoun in حُبِّهِ remains open; food, the act, and a God-directed reading do not generate identical baselines.
The ء س ر echo between captive and bodily frame may be deliberate activation or ordinary polysemy without cross-reference.
The seed-to-yield and mercy-versus-withholding models depend on reader-supplied material arrows and should remain exploratory.
The later reward may answer the entire righteous conduct cluster rather than the feeding act alone.
